correctness.rationale: For every partition Π into k blocks and vertex v in class A_i, every distance from v to a block is 0 for its own block, 2 for an OTHER block entirely in A_i, otherwise 1. Let c_i count pure blocks. Then the number of 2 entries is c_i−1 or c_i according as the own block is pure or mixed, so only two codes can occur per class. If the partition resolved all vertices each part size is at most 2. Each part of size 2 then needs one pure singleton (code q=0) and one mixed-block vertex (code q=1). Every singleton class likewise has q=0. With at least two classes, two vertices across classes have the identical sorted code {0,1^(k−1)}, contradiction. Independent full graph-distance enumeration tested every set partition of all 31 noncomplete connected multipartite profiles through order 7 (13,538 partitions); no resolving partition. This is corroboration, not proof for unbounded class size.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for the newly introduced multiset partition invariant on the entire canonical complete multipartite graph family. Its genuinely multiset-specific pure/mixed block collision argument resolves all sizes and subsumes all stars and complete bipartite graphs beyond the original K_n obstruction. The fact is an exact structural obstruction useful when deciding which families admit any resolving multiset partition; not a gratuitous parameter slice.

limitations: Only connected complete multipartite graphs with at least two parts, excluding the known all-singleton complete graphs.
The distinct invariant md(G) is not used as a shortcut to mpd(G).
